current_project_meta.name: mcmc-from-scratch
current_project_meta.title: MCMC from Scratch: Metropolis-Hastings, HMC and the Diagnostics
current_project_meta.description: Where the particle filter project points. Markov chain Monte Carlo built from scratch in NumPy - random-walk Metropolis and its scaling with dimension, Hamiltonian Monte Carlo with a leapfrog integrator and the energy error that makes the accept step almost free, the convergence diagnostics (R-hat, effective sample size, divergences) and whether each one detects the failure it is sold for, on targets whose exact answers are known and on Neal's funnel where they are known to fail
daily_plan: Target distributions with closed-form moments, random-walk Metropolis, detailed balance checked numerically, and the 0.234 acceptance-rate result measured rather than cited
Why random-walk mixing degrades with dimension, autocorrelation time and the integrated ESS, and independence-sampler and preconditioned proposals as the fixes that only sometimes work
Hamiltonian Monte Carlo - leapfrog integration, volume preservation and reversibility as testable identities, the energy error/acceptance relationship, and step-size and trajectory-length tuning
Neal's funnel, where HMC fails and says so via divergences, R-hat and split-R-hat against a chain that has visibly not converged, the non-centred reparameterisation, project README

completed_projects.name: particle-filter-nonlinear
completed_projects.title: Particle Filtering for Nonlinear State-Space Models
completed_projects.description: Where the Kalman project stops. Sequential Monte Carlo built from scratch in NumPy - the bootstrap filter on a nonlinear, non-Gaussian state-space model, weight degeneracy and the effective sample size, systematic versus multinomial resampling, the particle smoother, and a comparison against the extended and unscented Kalman filters on the same tracks
daily_plan: A nonlinear state-space model where the Gaussian belief is genuinely wrong, importance sampling as the base case, and the bootstrap filter - propagate, weight, resample
Weight degeneracy and effective sample size, systematic vs multinomial vs stratified resampling, and the variance each one contributes
The extended and unscented Kalman filters on the same model, and where each one's Gaussian assumption breaks against the particle posterior
Backward-simulation particle smoothing, likelihood estimation and its unbiasedness, RMSE and coverage against the exact filter on a linear model, project README

completed_projects.name: epistemic-uncertainty-ensembles
completed_projects.title: Epistemic Uncertainty: Deep Ensembles, MC Dropout and Laplace
completed_projects.description: The other half of the uncertainty the MDN project did not model - a mixture density network reports the spread of the data and reports it just as confidently where there is no data at all. Deep ensembles, MC dropout and a last-layer Laplace approximation built from scratch in PyTorch, separated into aleatoric and epistemic components on a dataset with a deliberate gap in its input range, and scored on whether the epistemic part actually grows where the training data stops
daily_plan: A regression dataset with a hole in it, a heteroscedastic Gaussian head, and the decomposition of predictive variance into aleatoric and epistemic parts - plus the demonstration that a single network reports near-zero uncertainty inside the hole

Deep ensembles - independent runs from different initializations, the mixture their predictions form, and whether disagreement between members is a usable epistemic signal or mostly initialization noise
MC dropout as approximate variational inference, the dropout-rate/lengthscale correspondence, and a last-layer Laplace approximation via the Gauss-Newton Hessian
Scoring them against each other - NLL and CRPS inside and outside the gap, calibration curves, the cost of each method in training runs, project README

completed_projects.description: An MDN built from scratch in PyTorch - a network emitting the parameters of a Gaussian mixture rather than a point estimate, trained by negative log-likelihood, on inverse problems where the conditional distribution is genuinely multimodal and a squared-error regressor averages the modes into a wrong answer
daily_plan: The inverse-problem dataset where least squares fails, and why a point regressor lands between the modes rather than on one
Mixture head with softmax weights and softplus scales, the log-sum-exp mixture NLL, and the numerical traps in it
Training, mode collapse and variance underflow, sampling from the predictive mixture, calibration against the true conditional, project README
